summary: Engineer with statistics background argues that GME's price has been controlled by a legacy high-frequency trading algorithm since 2002, recycling patterns across decades and constraining price movements to specific values. Claims the algorithm cannot be modified without triggering systemic collapse, predicts mini-squeezes based on dividend-date cycles and pattern-matching, and speculates that 2021 data was 'prewritten' from historical templates. Makes extensive use of price/volume data visualization and frequency analysis to support thesis that retail investors lack real market influence.

key_claims.claim: Claims that GME's price has been controlled by high-frequency trading algorithms since December 2002, when such algorithms were first introduced.
key_claims.note: No direct evidence of control mechanism; inferred from volume and price-action clusters. By 2026, no regulatory findings supported persistent algorithmic price control at the scale claimed. Pages 29-32.

key_claims.claim: Claims that open and close prices are manipulated to hit specific values (ending in .00, .25, .50) with statistically improbable frequency.
key_claims.note: Data shows genuine clustering of .25 multiples in 2021 and 2002-2003 (≈21% of total 1,552 instances). However, concentration alone does not prove intentional manipulation; could reflect market-maker rounding, technical levels, broker defaults. Pages 26-28.

key_claims.claim: Claims that price patterns from 2002-2003 mirror those from 2019-2021, indicating algorithmic reuse and predictability.
key_claims.note: Pattern-matching presented without rigorous statistical pattern-detection tests. Similarity is subjective; by 2026 GME's 2021-2024 price action was volatile and did not follow predicted algorithmic repeats. Pages 35-39.

key_claims.claim: Claims that the same HFT algorithm from 2002 is still operating in 2021 and cannot be changed due to legacy code complexity and lack of original programmers.
key_claims.note: HFT technology evolved significantly 2002–2021. Unfalsifiable claim that system cannot be modified without crash; no evidence by 2026 that GME remained locked into a 2002-era algorithm. Pages 12, 37.

key_claims.claim: Claims that quarterly volatility and mini-squeezes are driven by algorithmic response to historical dividend dates, predicting next mini-squeeze on November 23, 2021.
key_claims.note: Predictions on specific dates were not tracked as confirmed/failed in available record. Dividend theory rests on assumption that algo still reacts to discontinued-dividend cycles. Pages 11-12.

key_claims.claim: Claims that volume spikes represent hedge fund algorithmic activity rather than organic retail buying.
key_claims.note: Author infers non-organic activity from magnitude but provides no mechanism to distinguish HFT flows from retail; assumes retail buying is less likely to produce sudden volume outliers. Pages 19-21.

key_claims.claim: Claims that naked shorts remain hidden in the system and must eventually be covered, and that the algorithm prevents covering without exposing a crash.
key_claims.note: Short interest fell from 122% (Jan 2021) to ~20% by Feb 2021 and remained low through 2026. SEC October 2021 report found no evidence of widespread hidden shorting. DRS reach ~75M shares by mid-2023 without triggering squeeze. Pages 11-12 (implicit).

key_claims.claim: Claims that all of 2021 price data has been 'prewritten' based on planarized historical patterns.
key_claims.note: 2021 was highly volatile with unpredictable external events (media attention, options expiry, SEC statements). Data planarization is a visualization technique, not evidence of deterministic prediction. Pages 36-40.

validity_rationale: The book uses genuine market data and performs real statistical analysis, raising it above pure speculation. However, it commits persistent logical fallacies: conflating correlation with causation (price clustering = algorithmic control), cherry-picking pattern matches across decades, and making unfalsifiable claims. Core predictions (MOASS, persistent hidden shorts, November 23 squeeze) were falsified by hindsight. No evidence emerged of the alleged control mechanism or system fragility."
